claims.text: No tx needed for immunocompetent pts who are asymptomatic or have mild, uncomplicated acute infection.
claims.quote: No treatment is required for immunocompetent patients who are asymptomatic or have mild, uncomplicated acute toxoplasmosis.

claims.text: Most effective regimen (immunocompetent w visceral involvement or severe/persistent Sx): pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine, for 2 to 4 weeks.
claims.quote: The most effective regimen in immunocompetent patients with visceral involvement or severe or persistent symptoms is pyrimethamine plus sulfadiazine, for 2 to 4 weeks.

claims.text: Give leucovorin (folinic acid) concurrently to help protect against bone marrow suppression.
claims.quote: Leucovorin (folinic acid) is given concurrently to help protect against bone marrow suppression.

claims.text: Leucovorin, not folate: folate blocks the therapeutic effect. Monitor CBC weekly even w leucovorin.
claims.quote: Pyrimethamine bone marrow suppression can be minimized with leucovorin, also called folinic acid (but not folate, which blocks the therapeutic effect). Even when leucovorin is given, the complete blood count should be monitored weekly.

claims.text: Sulfonamide hypersensitivity: clindamycin + pyrimethamine + leucovorin; or atovaquone + pyrimethamine + leucovorin.
claims.quote: In patients who have or develop sulfonamide hypersensitivity, clindamycin is given with pyrimethamine and leucovorin instead of sulfonamides. Another option is atovaquone plus pyrimethamine and leucovorin.

claims.text: Pregnancy: spiramycin used safely to reduce fetal transmission during the first 18 weeks.
claims.quote: Spiramycin has been used safely to reduce transmission to the fetus in pregnant patients with acute toxoplasmosis during the first 18 weeks of pregnancy

claims.text: Pyrimethamine is a potent teratogen: don't use in the first or early second trimester.
claims.quote: NOTE: Pyrimethamine is a potent teratogen and should not be used during the first or early second trimester.
